$comment: A worked example for the commonest shape: one Node package at the repository root, pnpm scripts.
COPY IT, do not edit it in place -- the underscore prefix is load-bearing. Both the gate hook and
gate.sh skip files starting with '_', so nothing here can ever gate a real repository by accident.
That is also why it is safe to ship: an example profile that could match would be a set of
commands chosen by somebody else running at your turn end.
then set match.remote, and replace the commands with the ones your repository actually has.
Everything below is only a plausible default. A check that names a script your package.json does
not have fails every turn, which teaches you to ignore the gate -- the one outcome worse than
having no gate. /da-verify walks through authoring this, and reference/profile-authoring.md in
match.remote is spelled without an owner on purpose, so the profile follows the repository into
forks and clones. Pin it to 'owner/repo' instead when two repositories share a name.
